title: Programming a Computer for Playing Chess
summary: Claude E. Shannon published Programming a Computer for Playing Chess in Philosophical Magazine in March 1950, describing how a general-purpose computer could be programmed to play chess through move selection and position evaluation rather than exhaustive enumeration of every possible continuation.
significance: A documented early computer-chess paper that framed chess as a programming and search problem for general-purpose digital computers, providing a historically useful pre-Dartmouth record of machine problem-solving research.
